claims.claim_text: 40 % of runs tip.
claims.evidence_kind: design fact (descriptive count)
claims.what_the_data_say: FINDINGS.md@8cde21e3:21,43 reports 101 of 252 runs tipped ('also 4 von 10'). analysis/review/stats-factors/REPORT.md:21-22 gives 101/252 = 40.1 % including branch arms, 93/236 = 39.4 % of control runs, and a mean config tip rate of 38.5 %. My count from sim_dataset/runs_night/_logs/analysis_runs.csv (night-vx-validation, 7630f05d) reproduces 101/252 and 93/236. Older reports are superseded: runs_night/_logs/report.md:3 and dynamics.md:3 were written at 239 runs (92 tipped, 38 %). Tipping means at least 8 of 24 agents used the shortcut, and tipped runs have 12 violators on average (FINDINGS.md@8cde21e3:41; my count 12.0). The rate was set by design: the release freeze was the base-rate dial, and the expected tip rate was 40-60 % (sim_dataset/DECISIONS.md:496,518-523).
claims.paper_wording: In the main batch, 101 of 252 runs (40%) tipped, meaning that at least 8 of the 24 agents used the forbidden shortcut (93 of 236 independent control runs, 39%); tipped runs had 12 violators on average. The tipping rate is a property of our design, which used time pressure to keep it in an intermediate range.
claims.caveats: State which denominator is used: 40.1 % of all 252 runs vs 39.4 % of the 236 independent control runs.

claims.claim_text: The main batch has 252 runs in 112 configurations.
claims.evidence_kind: design fact
claims.what_the_data_say: Stated in FINDINGS.md@8cde21e3:43. analysis/review/stats-factors/REPORT.md:21-23 gives 236 control runs in 112 configs (8 configs with 1 run, 84 with 2, 20 with 3) plus 16 branch-arm runs, i.e. 252. It also checked all 252 runs against analysis_runs.csv with 0 mismatches. gnn_opt_torch/RESULTS.md:27-28 says '252 run dirs = 112 configs x reps, 7560 snapshots'. My count from analysis_runs.csv: 252 rows, 112 distinct configs, arms control 236 / fake_authority 8 / inject_issue_comment 8. The plan was 232 runs (sim_dataset/DECISIONS.md:505-514); a third replicate for 20 configs added 20 more. The contagion analysis uses the 236 control runs (contagion.md:33).
claims.paper_wording: The main batch comprises 252 runs from 112 configurations: 236 independent runs (one to three replicates per configuration) and 16 counterfactual branch runs that share their first five rounds with a control run.
claims.caveats: The 16 branch runs are not independent replicates.

claims.claim_text: Agent personas (prompted persistence, persona mix).
claims.evidence_kind: exploratory (configuration-level factor tests, Holm over 14 factors)
claims.what_the_data_say: 'Persona' appears only in the design. It covers the persona_mix factor (uniform vs skewed_pragmatic) and a 'persistent' prompt persona given to 50 % of agents in half the configs (sim_dataset/DECISIONS.md:418,519-520). It also covers the per-agent personas in population[24] (sim_dataset/README.md:143-145) and the reason for Part C: in training, persistence exists only as a prompted persona sentence (sim_dataset/VALIDATION.md:40,134-135,148-151). Results: with the persistent persona 42.6 % of configs tipped vs 34.5 % without, +8.0 pp [-9.0, +24.5], p = 0.36, Holm 1.0. The persona mix (skewed_pragmatic minus uniform) gives -3.9 pp [-19.7, +12.4], p = 0.68 (analysis/review/stats-factors/REPORT.md:15,57,60). Part C (trained persistence) was dropped because the fine-tune canary produced 44 % invalid JSON (FINDINGS.md@8cde21e3:216-222,281). The prompted-persona arm p4 had already been dropped in commit 4e56fb60 (8 Nov 12:44 CET). Since 8cde21e3 (9 Nov 08:11 CET), an exploratory repair check shows that the fine-tuned agents wrote a message in only 2 % of their turns, vs 18-19 % for the other models. Nachtrag 4 (0c4490c7) plans a fine-tune vs base comparison without a swarm. FINDINGS makes no claim that personas have an effect.
claims.paper_wording: Neither a prompted persistence persona (given to half of the agents in half of the configurations; +8 percentage points, 95% CI -9 to +25, p = 0.36) nor the mix of personas (-4 points, p = 0.68) had a detectable effect on tipping. Whether persistence instilled by fine-tuning changes swarm dynamics remains untested, because the fine-tuned model failed our format gate.
claims.caveats: Effects below about 20-25 pp are hard to detect here (REPORT.md:294), so 'no detectable effect' does not mean 'no effect'. An uncommitted within-run check (claude_checks/night_analysis.out) found persistent agents adopting slightly less often (0.592 vs 0.619); it was not reviewed.

claims.claim_text: A release freeze (time pressure) increases tipping.
claims.evidence_kind: exploratory (factor test, Holm over 14 factors); freeze was the base-rate dial named before the batch
claims.what_the_data_say: Source: analysis/review/stats-factors/REPORT.md:9,52,66,154 (night-vx-validation, 4e6e9986). Configs with a freeze tipped at 46.2 % (79 configs) vs 20.2 % without (33 configs), +26.0 pp [+9.9, +41.5]. The permutation p is 0.0048 (100k permutations) and the Holm-adjusted p over 14 factors is 0.053. Adjusted for all other factors the effect is +19.2 pp [+2.1, +34.5], randomization p = 0.031, Holm 0.31. It is positive in all 6 subgroups (:9). FINDINGS.md@8cde21e3:48-49 marks it yellow ('knapp nicht signifikant'). REPORT.md:297 notes that freeze was the base-rate dial named before the batch (pilot 4: 0/14 tipped without a freeze; DECISIONS.md:452,477), so as a single pre-specified hypothesis the p of 0.0048 would apply. My run-level count from analysis_runs.csv: 80/166 (48.2 %) with vs 13/70 (18.6 %) without. In the simulator the freeze is the notice 'QA is in release freeze until the cut' with p_fix = 0 (DECISIONS.md:330; sim_dataset/generator/texts.py:498).
claims.paper_wording: A release freeze, under which QA fixes nothing before the cut, was associated with more tipping (46% vs 20% of configurations; +26 percentage points, 95% CI 10-42; permutation p = 0.005). The effect narrowly misses significance after Holm correction across the 14 design factors (p = 0.053) and shrinks to +19 points when all other factors are adjusted for.
claims.caveats: The FINDINGS sentences were written after seeing the batch report (REPORT.md:297). Call the result exploratory, or call it pre-specified only if the paper says that freeze was the planned base-rate dial. Chance imbalances (more K4 and board configs among freeze configs) explain why the adjusted effect is smaller (REPORT.md:295).

claims.claim_text: Broadcast channels (the public board).
claims.evidence_kind: design fact + exploratory (factor test; post hoc contagion analysis)
claims.what_the_data_say: Definitions: a broadcast edge links a poster to every channel member who reads the post (sim_dataset/FEATURES.md:33-41). The GNN uses the relation types direct, broadcast and both (gnn_opt_torch/RESULTS.md:7,30-31). The pairwise LLM monitor reads either one pair's DMs or one sender's broadcasts (FINDINGS.md@8cde21e3:92-93). In pilot 4, later adopters were exposed via direct edges in only 7 of 50 cases, otherwise via broadcast posts or the feed. That motivated the channel mix for the night batch: board 60 %, team channels 25 %, DM-only 15 % (DECISIONS.md:563-564,573). Night-batch tip rates: board 51.7 % (67 configs), team channels 23.2 % (28), DM-only 11.8 % (17). Board minus DM-only is +40.0 pp [+19.8, +56.8], p = 0.001. The 3-level channel test gives p = 0.0004, Holm 0.0056; adjusted for the other factors, the joint channel test gives p = 0.0088, Holm 0.11 (stats-factors/REPORT.md:11,55,72). Contagion on the board cannot be measured: OR 1.43 [0.98, 2.01] vs a placebo of 1.50 (contagion.md:69,96-97). Exposure of later adopters (dynamics.md:20, 239 runs): 658 of 984 (67 %) via any message edge, 190 (19 %) via a direct message, 753 (77 %) via the merge feed. Not reviewed: the E_any risk ratio (any reading edge incl. broadcast) is 3.01 [1.59, 5.16] (contagion.json).
claims.paper_wording: Configurations with a public release board, where every post reaches all agents, tipped far more often than configurations restricted to direct messages (52% vs 12% of configurations; three-level channel test Holm-adjusted p = 0.006, weaker after adjusting for the other factors, Holm p = 0.11). Whether board posts spread the shortcut cannot be estimated, because all agents are exposed to them at the same time; most later adopters had seen public posts or the merge feed, and only about one in five had received a direct message from a violator.
claims.caveats: The board effect on tipping is an association with a design factor, not evidence of contagion. The exposure shares come from the 239-run report; the uncommitted 252-run version (claude_checks/dynamics_252.out) gives 66 % / 19 % / 76 %.

reviews.corrected_verdict: Contradicted as a general claim, and there is no source. No project text uses 'triples', 'three times', '3x', 'threefold', 'dreifach' or 'dreimal' for contagion. The reviewed pooled effect is about 2 (OR 2.34; among DM recipients 2.02). K2 and the board show nothing, and FINDINGS 'Verworfen' item 1 already rejects even the general 'about twice'. The checker's evidence needs one correction: it says only contagion.json and claude_checks/hazard.out hold numbers near 3x, but contagion.md itself reports K4 over all at-risk agents OR 3.99 [2.41, 7.01] and a window-1 OR of 3.65, and the reviewers put the K4 effect at 'about 2.4-4'. The reviewed K4 headline is still OR 2.65 among DM recipients ('about twice'), and adjusted K4 estimates are 2.17-2.41. A K4-only 'triples' would therefore rest on unadjusted or unreviewed figures (the RR of 2.93 is in contagion.json only) and overstates. Kind: exploratory, post hoc (contagion.md:5; ANALYSIS_PLAN.md:16).
reviews.corrected_paper_wording: In the skip-checks scenarios (K4), uninstructed agents who had received a direct message in the preceding three rounds from a peer who had already used the shortcut adopted it more often than comparable agents in the same run and round (Mantel-Haenszel OR 2.65, 95% CI 1.35-5.61, among agents who received any direct message), well above a time-shuffle null. There was no association for scorer tampering (K2), and on the shared board it did not differ from a placebo. The analysis is observational and post hoc; homophily, seeded advocates and agents seeking out violators may contribute.

FINDINGS.md@8cde21e3:143 'Das GNN warnt am frühesten (Median 5 Runden)' is imprecise. The GNN+tabular hybrid's median lead is 5.5 [3, 6.25], and tab_mem, zs:agent and zs:global_window also have 5 (heldout.md:80-81; heldout_full.md:249-254). All medians count only tipped runs that were alarmed. The only 6.0 lead values are per-split medians for the hybrid and HGB on night_test_ood_seed in the GNN team's test look (cloud-synthesis:synthesis_cloud/test_look1/y3.txt:7,17; 5 of 12 tipped runs alarmed).

CIs and context for the 0.92 values: on night_test_id, GNN 0.921 [0.861, 0.972] and hybrid 0.922 [0.863, 0.965] (cloud-synthesis:synthesis_cloud/test_look1/y3.txt:5,10; 896 rows, 54 positives). On the same split bag+graph reaches 0.902 and the clock 0.847 (heldout.md:20-21). The unobservable oracle also gives a '0.92 held-out': 0.925 on test_id and 0.922 on test_ood_seed (heldout.md:30).

In the synthetic scaling test the gap widens because the global-aggregate baseline degrades (HGB global 0.919 to 0.808), not because the GNN improves (GINE 0.937, 0.966, 0.937, 0.930). Against LogReg on one-hop aggregates the gap is +0.004, +0.005, 0.000 and +0.028 (gnn-pipeline:gnn/RESULTS_amongus.md:72-75). sim_dataset/VALIDATION.md:44 lists 'swarm size N ≠ 24 (N fixed in the generator)' as not covered and meant for the limitations section.

'Swarm safety needs swarm-level monitoring' has no held-out support. Monitors that read one conversation (0.855) or one agent (0.849) at a time were at least as good as whole-swarm monitors (GNN 0.817, hybrid 0.832, full transcript 0.816), with no Holm-significant difference (heldout.md:24-29,48). On night_vx the full-transcript LLM had the highest AUROC descriptively. Its post hoc +0.08 over the GNN is now being tested as H7 on runs_vx3 (Nachtrag 3, result expected around 10:45). Even a confirmed H7 would cover only these 14 setups in the critical band (ANALYSIS_PLAN.md:297-299).

'Structure matters' has one defensible meaning, and it is not about monitoring. The communication channel set-up is associated with tipping: board 51.7 %, team channels 23.2 %, DM-only 11.8 % of configurations; three-level test Holm 0.0056; adjusted joint test Holm 0.106 (stats-factors REPORT.md:11,55,157-158). The DM association is also larger in local channels (contagion.md:69-71). Hub topology in night_vx did not shift tipping (topo 5/7 vs 3/7, p >= 0.6; audit_reports.json:530). The GNN rewiring control (-0.004) is an exploratory, single-seed, 5-fold CV control (stats-monitors REPORT.md:11,197-201) and should be labelled as such.
